# Execution lease tenant scope, 2026-10-04

The actual integrated d5b whole-unit run retained 17,927 passing, one failing and 559 skipped cases. Its static SQL tenancy audit found that `operations.acquireExecutionLease` initially locked a lease by scope without binding a workspace. This source packet preserves that failed receipt and changes only the canonical native repository, its existing first-source PostgreSQL test and this handoff.

The repository validates and captures the required workspace, scope, holder and existing TTL bounds before its first await. Its initial lease lock binds both workspace and scope. An absent owning row reserves only a genuinely new scope with the existing native lease columns, first fence and database clock values. `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` never adopts a NULL or foreign tenant row. A concurrent insert is rechecked through the same owning lock; a genuine owning row reaches the existing same-holder renewal or acquisition logic, while a foreign or NULL collision refuses before either operation.

New insertion, renewal/acquisition and the unchanged native binder remain one transaction, in lease then operation lock order. Failed binding rolls back a newly inserted lease. The binder still requires an exact running live workflow claim, proposal digest, environment, workspace, worker holder and fence; it never consumes another approval, replaces a recorded pair, replays an uncertain execution or changes plain/reconcile lease behavior. There is no SQL audit waiver, tenancy exemption, public authority flag, generic lease API change or migration.

Seven additive required PostgreSQL identities cover missing workspace; live, expired and released foreign collisions; expired NULL collision; a foreign insertion between the actual absent owning lock and native reservation; and two genuine owning acquisitions crossing that absent-row collision. Native wrappers delay actual query results for the two race controls, using independent PostgreSQL connections and existing consumed human approval rows. They preserve the binding, every retained lease column and approval rows on refusal, and one same-holder fence on owning retry. The original 24 identities and callback bytes remain unchanged, with the same `ZENITH_TEST_FIRST_SOURCE_LEASE_REQUIRED=1` and canonical schema13 prerequisites. These are unrun source controls, with no Temporal, provider or live product proof.

Root must independently review this exact source freeze, run pinned Node22 compiler/lint and the existing SQL scoping audit, then execute the required native first-source suite and canonical PostgreSQL gate. The canonical gate needs the seven new identities only after source integration; the separate four-path G2 registration packet will add them without dropping its existing requirements. Author imports, compiler, tests, services, Docker, databases and commits are unrun. Preserve the prior source and failed whole-gate receipts; this packet supplies no runtime acceptance.
